Phishing.title: Phishing
Phishing.desc: Phishing is a method where fraudsters pretend to be a bank or a trusted organization to steal your data.
Phishing.example1: You receive an email: “Your account will be blocked, log in urgently”.
Phishing.example2: You click the link and enter your login and password.
protect: Do not enter data on unknown websites
Phishing.important: Banks never ask for your data via email or suspicious links.

Sms.title: SMS phishing
Sms.desc: Fraud carried out through SMS messages.
Sms.example1: You receive a message: “You won money, click the link”.
Sms.example2: You click the link and enter your data.
Sms.important: If it sounds too good, it’s usually a scam.

Phone.title: Phone fraud
Phone.desc: Scammers call and pretend to be bank employees.
Phone.example1: You receive a call: “Your account is at risk”.
Phone.example2: They ask you to provide a code from SMS.
Phone.important: Real bank employees never ask for codes.

Malware.title: Malware
Malware.desc: Programs that install on your device and steal data.
Malware.example2: It gains access to your data.
Malware.important: A free app can cost you your data.

Skimming.title: Card skimming
Skimming.desc: Devices on ATMs that copy your card data.
Skimming.example2: Later money is withdrawn from your account.
Skimming.important: If an ATM looks suspicious, do not use it.

Password.title: Password hacking
Password.desc: Weak passwords are easy for scammers to guess.
Password.example2: Scammers gain access to your account.
Password.important: One password = risk for all accounts.

Wifi.title: Fake Wi-Fi
Wifi.desc: Fake networks used to steal data.
Wifi.example1: You connect to a Free WiFi network.
protect: Do not access banking on public Wi-Fi
Wifi.important: Free Wi-Fi can cost you money.

Social.title: Social media scams
Social.desc: Fake accounts pretending to be bank employees.
Social.example2: They ask for your personal data.
Social.important: Banks do not contact you via private messages.

Sim.title: SIM swapping
Sim.desc: Scammers gain access to your phone number.
Sim.important: Loss of signal may indicate an attack.

Invest.title: Investment fraud
Invest.desc: Promises of fast and guaranteed profit.
Invest.example1: “We will double your money in 3 days”.
Invest.example2: You send money and lose it.
Invest.important: If it sounds too good, it’s a scam.

SafetyTips.title: How to protect yourself
SafetyTips.desc: Practical tips that will help you protect yourself and your money from scammers.

data.title: Data and Passwords
items: Use strong passwords (at least 12 characters).
Enable two-factor authentication.
Do not save passwords in the browser.
Never share passwords or SMS codes.

devices.title: Devices and Software
items: Keep your operating system and apps updated.
Download apps only from official sources.
Use antivirus and regularly scan your device.
Lock your device with a PIN or fingerprint.

internet.title: Internet and Networks
items: Check website address (must start with https://).
Do not enter data on suspicious websites.
Avoid using open Wi-Fi when possible.
Use VPN on public networks.

social.title: Social Networks
items: Do not click suspicious links.
Do not add unknown people.
Do not share personal information publicly.
Set up profile privacy.

cards.title: Bank Cards
items: Never share CVV or SMS codes.
Enable transaction notifications.
Set limits for transfers and purchases.
Use a separate card for online shopping.

important.title: Important!
important.text: Scammers act quickly and rely on your inattention. Always verify information and avoid making decisions in a hurry.

Cases.title: Real cases
Cases.desc: Stories of people who have encountered scammers. Learn from other people’s experience so you don’t become a victim.

phishing.title: Account loss due to phishing
phishing.desc: A user received an email that looked like it was from a bank asking to urgently confirm data via a link. The website was fake and scammers stole account access.
phishing.mistake: The user did not verify the sender and entered data on a fake website.
phishing.avoid: Always check the sender, avoid email links, and use official bank websites only.

investment.title: Investment fraud
investment.desc: A user was offered a guaranteed profit platform. They invested money and saw fake growth, but the account was blocked when withdrawing.
investment.avoid: Check licenses, reviews, and never trust guaranteed profit.

call.title: “Bank” phone call
call.desc: A scammer pretended to be a bank employee and asked for an SMS code to stop a fake transaction.
call.mistake: Shared an SMS code with a stranger.
call.avoid: Never share codes. Call the bank using official numbers only.

social.title: Social media purchase scam
social.desc: A user sent money for a cheap product on social media. After payment, the seller disappeared.
social.mistake: Sent money to an unknown seller without guarantees.
social.avoid: Check reviews and avoid upfront payments.

wifi.title: Public Wi-Fi hack
wifi.desc: A user used public Wi-Fi and logged into banking. Data was intercepted.
wifi.mistake: Used public Wi-Fi for banking operations.
wifi.avoid: Do not use public Wi-Fi for sensitive actions and use VPN.

Cases.note: Scammers are constantly coming up with new schemes. Stay vigilant!

Articles.title: Liability for fraud under the laws of the Republic of Tajikistan
Articles.description: Fraud is the unlawful taking of another person’s property or money through deception or abuse of trust. In the Republic of Tajikistan, criminal liability is provided for this offense. Depending on the amount of damage and the circumstances of the crime, the punishment may range from a fine to imprisonment for up to 15 years.
Articles.subtitle: Description
Articles.desc1: The unlawful taking of another person’s property or money through deception, misleading information, or abuse of trust. It may involve fake documents, false identities, or digital tools such as online platforms and banking systems.
Articles.desc2: Secret theft of another person’s property without their knowledge and without deception. Usually committed in a hidden manner without direct contact with the victim.
Articles.desc3: The concealment of the illegal origin of money or assets obtained through criminal activity by using financial transactions, transfers, or third parties.
Articles.desc4: Unauthorized access to computer systems, databases, or banking accounts with the purpose of obtaining, modifying, or destroying information.
Articles.desc5: The creation, distribution, or use of malicious software intended to disrupt systems, steal data, or gain unauthorized access to financial resources.
Articles.note: The information is provided for educational purposes only. The exact legal classification of the act and the punishment are determined by the court.

About.card1Desc: The project helps users understand different types of fraud and how laws protect citizens.
About.card2Desc: We explain how scammers operate and how to avoid becoming a victim.
About.card3Desc: The platform covers international and local cybercrime patterns and prevention methods.
About.note: Information is provided for educational purposes only. Legal qualification is determined by the court.
